page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 processor provides 105 MB of Level 3 cache, 2 MB of Level 2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration via Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 vector extensions. Memory capacity measures 128 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, while offering a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps without dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position the m7i-flex.8xlarge within the upper quartile for single-threaded throughput, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 2023.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 32.42 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput also scores in the top 25% at 48.18 GB/sec. Multi-core performance aligns with the median across general-purpose profiles, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 15569.0, multi-core stress-ng at 32413.77, and PassMark database operations at 16314.4. Memory subsystems deliver 170.39 GB/sec read and 89.67 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. While the system handles small LLM text generation efficiently due to AMX and AVX-512 extensions, large-scale model inference scales poorly, registering bottom-quartile throughput on 70B parameter models.

The m7i-flex tier uses a burstable CPU allocation designed to provide cost-effective general compute by leveraging excess capacity for workloads that do not continuously saturate 100% CPU utilization. This configuration delivers modern Intel 4th Gen Xeon performance and fast DDR5 memory at a lower baseline resource cost than fixed-performance compute tiers. Suitable workloads include containerized web services, distributed caching layers such as Redis, enterprise application backends, CI/CD compilation jobs, and data manipulation pipelines that require high memory bandwidth and solid single-thread performance without demanding persistent peak compute.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz with 128 GB of DDR5 memory. Utilizing the Nitro hypervisor on x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets. The server does not bundle local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and features a baseline network capacity of 6 Gbps without GPUs. Benchmark testing highlights top-quartile results in single-threaded operations such as gzip compression and web serving throughput, while multi-core compute, PassMark database tasks, and memory bandwidth tests track median performance levels. Built with a burstable CPU model, the m7i-flex.8xlarge optimizes resource expenditure for environments with variable compute demands, serving as an efficient host for web applications, Redis caching, microservices, and continuous integration pipelines.
